:::{#exr-transpose-product-practice}
#### Testing whether a transpose keeps the order of a product

A common slip in least-squares algebra
is to take the [transpose](#def-matrix-transpose) of a [product](#def-matrix-mult) without reversing the order of its factors.
Let

$$
\matr{A} = \sbmat{1 & 2 \\ 0 & 1},
\qquad
\matr{B} = \sbmat{1 & 0 \\ 3 & 1}.
$$

Is $\tp{(\matr{A}\matr{B})}$ [equal](#def-matrix-equality) to $\tp{\matr{A}}\,\tp{\matr{B}}$?

::: {.callout-tip}
#### Hint

Compute both sides with @def-matrix-mult and @def-matrix-transpose.
